Name: Areaportals in doorways
Description: Put an areaportal in the doorway of each door that has none, closing with the door, so a shut door hides everything behind it and the server stops sending what is there. Only openings framed by world brushes on all four sides are used, and only where the portal really divides two areas - a window or gap round the side rules a door out. Unnamed doors given a portal are named vw_door_<id>. Stays within the 191 areaportals Garry's Mod loads, counting the map's own, and keeps the ones that hide the most.
Warning: Adds names to doors that had none. Lua that finds doors by having no name would see them differently.

Name: Make detail
Description: Turn small and complex world brushes - trim, railings, pillars, stairs, frames - into func_detail, so they stop cutting the map into extra pieces for VVIS. Brushes that form the outside of the map, frame an areaportal, are water or are in a visgroup named viswright_ignore are never touched. Any brush a leak runs through goes back to being world, and the whole pass is undone if collision changes or more becomes visible.

Name: Hide covered faces
Description: Make faces nodraw when they are pressed flat against an opaque solid brush and so can never be seen - mainly world faces behind func_detail, which VBSP does not remove itself. Saves faces and lightmap space. A face is only changed when all of it is proven covered.

Name: Fade static props
Description: Give static props that never fade a fade distance: where the prop shrinks to a few pixels on a 1080p screen at a 90 degree field of view. Props that already fade, props in the 3D skybox, large landmark props, models marked never to fade, and props whose fade would lie beyond the map are left alone. Every model and its distance is listed in the output.
Warning: Changes how far props are drawn. The default of 6 pixels is chosen so nobody notices; raise Fade pixels for a bigger saving with some popping.

Name: Fade pixels
Description: How small a prop must look before it fades: 6 is conservative, 10 balanced, 16 aggressive. Only used with Fade static props.

Name: Fewer entities
Description: Turn prop_dynamic that nothing names, parents, fires, animates or lets the physgun move into prop_static, and plain always-solid func_brush into func_detail, freeing edicts and network traffic. A func_brush is only changed when it already casts a lightmap shadow, so lighting stays the same. Classes that the game's gamemodes, addons or the Lua folders below look up by class are left alone.
Warning: Converted entities no longer exist as entities. Lua that finds them some other way than by class would not find them.

Name: Lua folder
Description: A folder of Lua - a gamemode or addons outside the game folder - to check before Fewer entities converts anything. The game's own gamemodes and addons are always checked.

Name: Hints over open ground
Description: Try hint brushes across open streets and courtyards at a few heights above the ground, and keep one only where it lowers what players standing there can see. Each height costs a VBSP and VVIS compile, so this needs VVIS++ and stops searching when Hint search minutes run out. Hints are never solid or drawn and cannot leak; the set is undone unless the whole map sees less.
Warning: Adds several compiles to every run - about a minute each on a large map - until the search time runs out.

Name: Hint search minutes
Description: How long Hints over open ground may spend compiling to search. Only used with Hints over open ground.

Name: VBSP block size
Description: The -blocksize the VBSP step uses, so Viswright's checking compiles cut the map the same way. Leave off for VBSP's default of 1024; stock VBSP has no -blocksize.

Name: Write a review
Description: Write a review of everything Viswright did and considered beside the optimised copy: a VMF to open in Hammer++ with every change, refusal and a visibility heatmap in a Viswright visgroup and a camera on each top item, plans of every floor showing what is visible before and after, a picture of each top item, and a page listing them all with the reason for each, and PVS slack: how much of what each place's PVS lets through cannot be seen from there, found by casting rays on the GPU. Adds one VBSP and VVIS compile and the time to draw the plans.

Name: Cast rays on the CPU
Description: Measure the review's PVS slack on the CPU even when there is a GPU. The GPU is about ten times faster and casts four times as many rays; the CPU is used anyway when no GPU with Direct3D 12 is found.

Name: Accept the review
Description: Accept every item the last review left waiting, after taking in what you changed in the review VMF in Hammer (deleted changes are denied, moved hints and areaportals are kept where you put them, markers in Viswright/Accept are accepted). From then on compiles apply exactly the accepted items, with no search. Untick it once the map is decided.

Name: Mode
Description: Leave off for the usual flow: a review on a map's first run (the compile uses the map as it is), pinned once every item is decided. auto searches and applies whatever proves itself on every compile; review always reviews; pinned always applies the decided items.

Name: Report only
Description: Work out and report every change, but compile the map as it is.

Name: Thread limit
Description: Limit how many CPU cores Viswright uses. Leave this off to use all of them.
